question: After the death of Shivaji, which group came to hold effective political power in the Maratha state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chitpavan Brahmanas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• After the death of **Shivaji Maharaj** in **1680**, the Maratha Empire faced a period of political instability due to succession disputes and external invasions, especially by the **Mughals**.

• During this period, the **Chitpavan Brahmanas**, a community of Brahmins primarily located in the coastal regions of Maharashtra, rose to prominence and became influential in the Maratha administrative and political system.

• The **Peshwa system** (chief ministers) was established, and the **Chitpavan Brahmanas** dominated this position. The Peshwas became the de facto rulers of the Maratha Empire from the early 18th century.

• Notable Peshwas like **Baji Rao I** and **Nana Saheb** were instrumental in expanding the Maratha Empire and consolidating its governance under Brahmanical leadership.

• Under the leadership of the Peshwas, the **Chitpavan Brahmanas** controlled key administrative, military, and financial aspects of the Maratha state, ensuring their dominance in the political sphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Chitpavan Brahmanas:** 

• The Chitpavans were a community of Brahmins located primarily in the **Kokan region** of Maharashtra.

• They were known for their administrative skills, strategic thinking, and intellectual capabilities, which made them suitable for leadership roles in the Maratha Empire.

• They played a pivotal role in shaping the administrative and military policies of the Maratha state during the Peshwa era.

• Prominent Chitpavan Brahmanas like **Baji Rao I** were instrumental in establishing Maratha dominance across India, challenging the Mughal Empire.

• **Peshwa System:**

• The Peshwa system was established by **Shivaji Maharaj's successors** and became the hallmark of Maratha governance.

• Under the Peshwas, the Maratha Empire expanded significantly, reaching as far as Delhi in the north and Orissa in the east.

• Peshwas like **Baji Rao I** and **Madhav Rao** are celebrated for their military campaigns and administrative reforms.

• **Decline of Mughals:**

• After Shivaji's death, the **Mughals** tried to reassert control over the Deccan region but faced resistance from the Marathas.

• The decline of the Mughal Empire post-1707, especially after the death of **Aurangzeb**, provided an opportunity for the Marathas to establish their dominance.

• **Other groups in the Maratha Empire:**

• **Deshmukhs:** They were local landholders and administrators but did not achieve central political dominance like the Peshwas.

• **Kunbis:** A farming community that supported the Maratha movement but remained primarily agrarian and did not hold significant political power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Baji Rao I:** He was one of the most celebrated Peshwas and is remembered for his military genius and successful campaigns against the Mughals and other regional powers.

• **Madhav Rao:** A Peshwa known for his administrative reforms and efforts to stabilize the Maratha Empire during a period of internal and external turmoil.

• **Role of Chitpavan Brahmanas:** Their dominance in the Peshwa system highlights the socio-political dynamics of the Maratha Empire, where Brahmanical leadership played a key role.

• **Maratha Expansion:** Under the Peshwa leadership, the Marathas emerged as one of the most powerful entities in India, challenging the declining Mughal Empire and other regional states.
